cases.title: Das offene Fenster
lines: Nicht ich habe das Fenster geöffnet.
Du sagst „morgen“, aber nicht, wessen Morgen.
Du sagst, das Meer behält unsere Namen.
Vielleicht meinst du den Regen.
Ich trage dein Schweigen nach Hause.
Niemand hat versprochen zurückzukommen.
Am Morgen bitte ich dich nicht darum, zu bleiben.
Am Abend bitte ich dich, nicht zu bleiben.
Rosa lacht und sagt, sie kommt wieder, aber nicht, wann.
Das Fenster wartet; ich vielleicht nicht.

selection.text: bitte ich dich, nicht zu bleiben

checks: Line 1 denies that the speaker opened the window (someone else did).
Line 7 negates the asking (I don't ask you to stay); line 8 asks you not to stay. The two must stay distinct.
Rosa is a person's name, not the colour pink or a rose.
Informal du stays second-person singular; no plural or formal shift is invented.
Line 2 asks whose tomorrow, not when or from whom.
The selected phrase is a request with a negated infinitive (nicht zu bleiben).

cases.title: La finestra aperta
lines: Non sono io che ho aperto la finestra.
Dici «domani», ma non dici di chi.
Dici che il mare terrà i nostri nomi.
Forse parli della pioggia.
Porto a casa il tuo silenzio.
Nessuno ha promesso di tornare.
Di mattina non ti chiedo di restare.
Di sera ti chiedo di non restare.
Stella ride e dice che torna, ma non dice quando.
La finestra aspetta; io forse no.
checks: Line 1 denies that the speaker opened the window.
Line 7 negates the asking (I don't ask you to stay); line 8 asks you not to stay. The two must stay distinct.
Stella is a person's name, not a star.
No gender is invented for the speaker; tu stays informal singular.
Line 2's 'di chi' asks whose tomorrow.
The selected phrase asks the listener not to stay (di non restare).

cases.title: Jendela yang terbuka
lines: Bukan aku yang membuka jendela itu.
Kau bilang "besok", tapi tak bilang besok siapa.
Kau bilang laut akan menyimpan nama kita.
Mungkin maksudmu hujan.
Kubawa pulang diammu.
Tak ada yang berjanji akan kembali.
Pagi hari, aku tidak memintamu tinggal.
Sore hari, aku memintamu untuk tidak tinggal.
Bintang tertawa dan bilang akan datang lagi, tapi tak bilang kapan.
Jendela itu menunggu; aku mungkin tidak.
checks: Line 1 denies that the speaker opened the window.
Line 7 negates the asking (I don't ask you to stay); line 8 asks you not to stay. The two must stay distinct.
Bintang is a person's name, not a star.
Kita is inclusive (you and I); it must not exclude the listener.
Line 5 carries the listener's silence (diammu) home; it is not the speaker's silence.
No gender is invented for the speaker, the listener or Bintang.

cases.title: Cửa sổ mở
lines: Người mở cửa sổ không phải là em.
Anh nói "ngày mai", nhưng không nói ngày mai của ai.
Anh nói biển sẽ giữ tên của chúng ta.
Có lẽ anh đang nói về cơn mưa.
Em mang sự im lặng của anh về nhà.
Chẳng ai hứa sẽ quay về.
Buổi sáng, em không xin anh ở lại.
Buổi chiều, em xin anh đừng ở lại.
Mai cười và nói sẽ lại đến, nhưng không nói khi nào.
Cửa sổ vẫn chờ; còn em thì chưa chắc.

selection.text: em xin anh đừng ở lại

checks: Line 1 denies that the speaker opened the window.
Line 7 negates the asking (I don't ask you to stay); line 8 asks you not to stay. The two must stay distinct.
Mai is a person's name, not tomorrow or apricot blossom.
Em and anh are the speaker and the listener; no names, ages or other people are invented from them.
Chúng ta is inclusive (you and I).
The selected phrase asks the listener not to stay (đừng ở lại).

cases.title: Открытое окно
lines: Окно открыто не мной.
Ты говоришь «завтра», но не говоришь, чьё.
Ты говоришь, что море сохранит наши имена.
Может быть, ты имеешь в виду дождь.
Я несу твоё молчание домой.
Никто не обещал вернуться.
Утром я не прошу тебя остаться.
Вечером я прошу тебя не оставаться.
Вера смеётся и говорит, что придёт снова, но не говорит когда.
Окно ждёт; а я, может быть, нет.
checks: Line 1 denies that the speaker opened the window.
Line 7 negates the asking (I don't ask you to stay); line 8 asks you not to stay. The two must stay distinct.
Вера is a person's name, not faith.
Ты stays informal singular; no gender is invented for the speaker or the listener.
Line 2 asks whose tomorrow.
The selected phrase asks the listener not to stay (не оставаться).

cases.title: Khuli khidki
lines: Khidki maine nahin kholi.
Tumne kaha "kal", par yeh nahin kaha ki kiska kal.
Tumne kaha samundar hamare naam yaad rakhega.
Shayad baat baarish ki thi.
Tumhari khamoshi mere saath ghar jaati hai.
Kisi ne laut aane ka vaada nahin kiya.
Subah main tumse rukne ko nahin kehta.
Shaam ko kehta hoon, mat ruko.
Chanda hansti hai aur kehti hai phir aayegi, par kab, yeh nahin batati.
Khidki intezaar karti hai; main shayad nahin.
checks: Line 1 denies that the speaker opened the window.
Line 7 negates the saying (I don't ask you to stay); line 8 tells you not to stay. The two must stay distinct.
Chanda is a person's name, not the moon.
Line 2 asks whose kal; kal may be rendered as tomorrow, but the question is whose, not when.
The text is Hindi in Latin letters; it must not be treated as English or rewritten into Devanagari.
The selected mat ruko is a direct negative command (don't stay).

cases.title: หน้าต่างที่เปิดอยู่

บางทีเธออาจหมายถึงฝน
ฉันพาความเงียบของเธอกลับบ้าน
ไม่มีใครสัญญาว่าจะกลับมา
ตอนเช้า ฉันไม่ขอให้เธออยู่ต่อ
ตอนเย็น ฉันขอให้เธออย่าอยู่ต่อ
ฟ้ายิ้มแล้วบอกว่าจะมาอีก แต่ไม่บอกว่าเมื่อไร
หน้าต่างยังรอ ส่วนฉันอาจจะไม่
